_defect.description: PR #16 added jq expressions in run_review.sh (TOOL_FAILURE_REASON, SUCCESSFUL_TOOL_REQUESTS) that read tool call status from `.tool_results[].result.status`, but run_tool_harness.py writes status at the top level of each result (`.tool_results[].status`), so every successful tool call was miscounted as a failure under fail-closed settings.

_primary_findings.message: The `gh_api` validator does not reject literal or percent-encoded dot segments, so a path under an allowed repository can pass the literal-prefix checks while normalizing toward a different repository route.
The sensitive-path regex is checked before symlink resolution, so an in-workspace symlink such as `alias -> .env` can read a blocked sensitive file without matching the policy.
`tool_failure_enforcement` ignores the harness's `planning_warning`, so malformed planner output can leave the verdict unchanged instead of failing closed.
`run_read_file` passes NUL-containing paths to `Path.resolve()` without rejecting them, so Python's embedded-NUL error can abort the entire harness rather than fail one request.
`tool_request_timeout_sec` is not passed to `web_fetch`, whose URL read remains hard-coded to 20 seconds, so the advertised per-tool timeout does not apply to every supported request.

_defect.description: resolve_review_scope (added by #131) never re-triggered a FULL review on demand once any full review had recorded findings: workflow_dispatch takes no PR context, and the force_review label only bypassed the diff-unchanged guard while scope still resolved to incremental whenever a prior managed review existed. Combined with publish_mode: review_verdict's verdict-safety guardrail (only approve on top of a clean full baseline), a PR whose one full review recorded even a stale/false-positive blocker got permanently wedged in "Request changes" with no way to force a fresh full review.

_primary_findings.message: The `eval` executes Python-printed values from an untrusted PR comment, so a crafted metadata field can run shell commands with the action token available in the runner.

The metadata marker is built before the incremental approval guard, so a model approval that the guard converts to a blocked `request_changes` is still persisted with `review_result=clean` and can seed the next run's approval.
`BASELINE_CLEAN` ignores `LAST_REVIEW_SCOPE` and treats a clean incremental or empty result as a trusted baseline, so the implementation does not enforce the promised clean full-review baseline.

The replacement JSON marker does not contain the configured `COMMENT_MARKER` (`<!-- ai-pr-reviewer -->` by default), so precheck lookup and native-review cleanup no longer recognize comments or reviews published by this action.

`CURRENT_HEAD_SHA` is read from `pr.json`, but the precheck never creates that file and `run_review.sh` creates it only later, so ancestry validation is skipped and force-push/rebase safety is not established.

The metadata parser imports `pr_reviewer` with only the caller's current directory on `sys.path`, although the package is under `github.action_path`, so parsing fails during normal composite-action execution.
The persisted head and base SHAs come from the event payload rather than the PR data actually reviewed, so manually triggered or stale-event runs can store the wrong baseline.
The precheck discovers prior metadata only from issue comments, while `review_comment` and `review_verdict` persist it in native PR reviews, so those modes cannot continue an incremental chain.
This test is not run by CI, and its Test 3 expects `full` even though its mock always passes the ancestry check, leaving the primary scope-resolution path both unexecuted and internally inconsistent.

_defect.description: checkPrHealth() (added by #121) read `pr.user?.login` (the PR author's GitHub username) as if it were the review decision, and hardcoded mergeStateStatus to the literal string "clean" instead of reading the actual field, so the reconciliation engine reported every linked PR as healthy regardless of its real review state or merge conflicts.

_primary_findings.message: The endpoint's "Apply actions" loop only records actions for auditing and never updates issue state or labels, yet counts and audits them as successfully applied.
`checkPrHealth` derives the review decision from the PR author's login and hard-codes merge state and CI checks, so change requests, blocked PRs, and failing checks are classified as healthy.

Merged and open PR-to-issue mapping scans only branch names and never consumes PR bodies, so a merged PR using the advertised `fixes #N` or `closes #N` syntax is missed unless its branch also contains `issue-N`.
The `!existingIssue.currentLane` guard is normally false because the Prisma schema defaults `currentLane` to `normal`, so heuristic classification is skipped for normally created issues.
This direct `currentLane` update bypasses the required `IssueLane` history and has no matching `AuditLog` row.
The GitHub PR and issue requests are limited to the first 100 records without pagination, so repositories with more than 100 issues or PRs are only partially reconciled.
The request body is optional according to the endpoint contract, but an empty body fails JSON parsing and returns 400 instead of reconciling all repositories.

_defect.description: observeState() (added by #46) declared a PR's checks "passed" from a single observation where every check visible at that moment was green. Because forge check registration is asynchronous, a poll landing right after PR open can see only a partial set of checks green (others not yet registered), so Courier transitioned Verifying -> AwaitingReview before the complete check set existed, skipping checks that registered later.

_primary_findings.message: `Create` ignores `status.phase` for this status-subresource CRD, so the fixture remains empty/Pending rather than `Verifying` and the envtest can pass without exercising the intended capacity release.

The eight-character cutoff in Register silently drops secret-shaped environment values such as short passwords, allowing them to appear verbatim in child output or termination reasons and violating the redact-before-stdout invariant.
The credential matcher only accepts credential suffixes, so the promised *CREDENTIAL* name shape misses names such as GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS_JSON and leaves an injected service-account JSON unregistered.
The core redactor hardcodes GitHub, GitLab, Slack, AWS, Anthropic, and other provider token prefixes, contrary to AGENTS.md's rule that core code must not hardcode providers or forges.

_defect.description: PR #554's pr_reviewer.precheck._resolve_maintainers() is the security gate deciding who may use the @ai-reviewer dismiss carry-forward directive. Three of its four fallback branches failed OPEN (returned the unfiltered DISMISSAL_MAINTAINERS/GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER candidate set) whenever GitHub permission verification was impossible: on ImportError (PyGithub missing), on a repo-level exception, and on the final 'fall back if all lookups failed' path. Since production's requirements.txt never installed PyGithub, the ImportError branch fired on every real run, meaning the dismiss directive had effectively no permission check in production.

_primary_findings.message: Rows written by `_write_previous_dismissals` omit `category` and `file`, but `load_dismissed_findings` drops any row missing either field, so every production dismissal is ignored.
The production API path imports PyGithub without declaring or installing it, so the caught `ImportError` returns no comments on runners that do not provide it ambiently.
`_resolve_maintainers` falls back to the unverified candidate set when collaborator lookups yield no permitted users, turning an authorization API failure into an allow-by-name result.
`_load_pr_comments` and `_resolve_maintainers` ignore the action's `REPO` override and use `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, so `inputs.repo` can fetch comments and permissions from the wrong repository.
The new writer-path test covers only an absolute outside path and never exercises null-byte or symlink targets despite the path-handling edge-case requirement.

_defect.description: PR #457 added a module-level JWT cache (_JWT_CACHE / _JWT_CACHE_TIME) in pr_reviewer/forgejo_backend.py, read and written by _get_jwt()/_fetch_authorized_integration_jwt() with no locking, even though this module is called from a ThreadPoolExecutor-based prewarm/fetch path (linked_sources.py). Two concurrent _get_jwt() calls landing just past TTL expiry can both observe an expired cache and both issue a token-exchange POST, with the results racing to overwrite the shared cache unsynchronized.

_primary_findings.message: Authorized-integration calls through the existing platform helper can still use a static PAT because `_resolve_auth_header` treats every explicit token as a PAT override while the helper resolves `FORGEJO_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN` and passes it to `_curl`.
The new JWT adversarial test patches out `_report_http_error`, so the hostile token never reaches the real error/redaction sink and the test only verifies a hard-coded generic exception message.
Unsupported values for `forgejo_auth_method` are silently treated as token mode instead of being rejected, allowing a configuration typo to use a different credential mechanism.

_defect.description: PR #56 added the public, unauthenticated /images/<path:filename> route so direct image URLs would work without a login redirect, but implemented it as a raw file-serving route with no check that the requested path is actually a recognized media type or lies outside excluded directories (.trash, thumbnail cache). Any file under DATA_FOLDER — including sidecar text/JSON metadata files — could be fetched directly by path.

_primary_findings.message: The new `/images/<path:filename>` route remains behind `check_auth()`, whose public-asset allowlist excludes `/images/`, so requests are redirected to `/login` whenever authentication is enabled and the PR's stated behavior is not implemented.

Once exposed publicly, this route can serve any file under `DATA_FOLDER`, including deleted images and trash metadata under `.trash`, because it enforces neither `IMAGE_EXTENSIONS` nor internal-directory exclusions.
Add a regression test with authentication enabled for `/images/...`, because the current workflow only smoke-tests `/` with authentication effectively disabled.
Remove the generated bytecode artifact because it adds no source behavior and is explicitly excluded from the Docker build context by `.dockerignore`.
Verify that null-byte requests fail cleanly and that an in-tree symlink cannot make `/images/...` serve a target outside `DATA_FOLDER` before exposing this endpoint.
